main_text.p: fassurũ esse omnẽ, qui orationis differentias scit dignoscere. Sensit idem Eusebius, qui suprà Hist.L.iii.C.xxxii. phrasim, esse illi Clementis cumprimis affinem dixit. Hieronymus, hoc uno nomine non credi Epistolam esse Pauli, propter styli, sermo-nisque dissonantiam. Itidem Philastrius, nempe quia utitur sermone nimium plau-sibili. Unius fere illius difficultatis quæ Latinos priores ad dissensum induxerit meminere pariter, Isidorus de Eccles. Of-fic. L.i.C.ix. Rabanus, de Instit. Cler. L.ii. C. LIV. Hinc quotquot Veterum pro paulo pronunciarunt, sive ex Græcis, sive Latinis Patribus, fere obviarunt eidem difficultati. Ex posterioribus nodū hunc plusquàm Gordium facit Erasmus, sub finem Annotat. Restat jam argumentum illud quo non aliud certius, stylus ipse & orationis character, qui nihil habet affi-nitatis cum phrasi Paulinà. Accedit & ipse Calvinus, Argum. in Epist. Magde-burgenses Cent.i.L.ii.Cap.iv. quotquot denique (ne faciam longius) in hac de Authore controversia à nobis discesserè.

page.notes: The "IV." at the lower right is placed as a gathering-type mark and has been set as a signature; it may instead be a section marker. The running head "Epistola" is partly illegible; the final letter is doubtful. The Roman numeral in "Hist.L.iii" is set in small type and read as lowercase iii. The spelling "Epistole" in the running head is uncertain. Section numbers and references are copied as printed.
